title: Worked Examples: Dose-Change Supply by Length of the Fill (Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit)
content:
**Rule.** For a dose-change override under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit, the dose-change supply depends on the length of the fill being re-dosed:

- for a fill of 61 days or more, it is the dose-change shortfall, so the member stays on the long fill's cycle;
- for a fill of 35 to 60 days, it is the dose-change shortfall rounded up to a whole multiple of 30 days;
- for a fill of 34 days or fewer, it is the days supply of the fill being re-dosed.

**The dose-change shortfall.** The days of the fill being re-dosed still left on the re-dosing date are re-counted at the new quantity per 30 days — multiplied by the old quantity per 30 days and divided by the new one, rounded down to whole days — and the dose-change shortfall is the days from the re-dosing date to the dose-change end date less those re-counted days, never below zero.

**Terms.** The days still left on the re-dosing date are the days from the re-dosing date to the day the fill's days supply runs out, counted from the day its days start, never below zero. The old quantity per 30 days is the fill's quantity multiplied by 30 and divided by its days supply. Where the new quantity per 30 days is zero, nothing is re-counted. The length of the fill is its days supply; a fill that counts zero days falls in the 34-days-or-fewer line.

## Worked example 1 (hypothetical): a 90-day fill

A 90-day retail fill of 90 tablets whose days start on day 0; the end date is day 90; the re-dosing date is day 30; the new quantity is 60 per 30 days.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Old quantity per 30 days | 90 multiplied by 30, divided by 90: 30 |
| Days left on day 30 | 90 less 30: 60 |
| Re-counted days | 60 multiplied by 30, divided by 60: 30 |
| Days from re-dosing date to end date | 90 less 30: 60 |
| Shortfall | 60 less 30: 30 |
| Dose-change supply (61 days or more) | 30 |

## Worked example 2 (hypothetical): a 60-day fill

A 60-day fill whose figures give a shortfall of 17 days: rounded up to a whole multiple of 30, the dose-change supply is 30. A shortfall of 31 days gives 60; a shortfall of zero gives zero.

## Worked example 3 (hypothetical): a 30-day fill

A 30-day fill: the dose-change supply is 30, whatever the shortfall.
